oh_salt_fork_state_park.blurb: Salt Fork State Park, in Guernsey County in eastern Ohio, is a bouldering area on sandstone that is solid and well featured, noticeably less crumbly than some other Ohio sandstone. All of the climbing is boulder problems, from the easy end up to V9; most land between V1 and V4, so moderates are plentiful, with a modest number of hard lines. The boulders sit in many separate groups through the woods. Pine Crest Trail Boulders, below a pine forest and above the lake, is the largest and best known, and Zephyr Road Boulders, PR-11 Boulders and Morgan's Knob Boulders add more. Many lines are still undeveloped.

ca_pie_shop_the.blurb: The Pie Shop is a crag-and-boulder area on the South Shore of Lake Tahoe, at about 6,300 feet. Bouldering is the biggest part, roughly half of the climbs, spread over a hillside, with sport, trad and a few top-rope lines on walls such as Main Wall, Middle Aged Wall and Space Invaders. Boulder problems run from V0 to V9, with most in the easier half. Roped routes run from 5.5 to 5.13, with many between 5.10 and 5.12. Sitting lower than much of Tahoe, it can be climbed during dry spells in winter. Tracking down a particular problem among the boulders takes some looking. Monty Python Castles is another sizeable section.

nv_black_velvet_canyon.blurb: Black Velvet Canyon is part of the Red Rock area of southern Nevada, where the walls are sandstone. Trad dominates, with long routes on Black Velvet Wall running to as many as 16 pitches, alongside a sizeable amount of bouldering and a few sport lines. Roped grades run from 5.6 to 5.13, centred on 5.10 and 5.11, and boulder problems range from V0 to V12. Red Rock sandstone is fragile when wet, so climbing waits for dry rock. Whiskey Peak is the biggest section, followed by Black Velvet Wall, Brown Warm Up Boulder and Texas Wall. The sandstone is relatively solid, with a hard surface varnish, and many routes follow long crack systems.

vt_bolton_bouldering.blurb: Bolton Bouldering is a woodland bouldering area in northern Vermont, about 30 minutes from Burlington, with problems spread over many small groups of boulders. Everything is boulder problems, from V0 to V11, with most between V1 and V4 and a smaller set of harder lines up to V10 and V11. Lines include seams and cracks, aretes and crimpy faces, and the feel is of being lost in the woods. It is often overlooked next to nearby Smugglers' Notch. Bolton Notch Rd Boulders is the largest group, at around 1,100 feet, ahead of Pinneo Brook Bouldering, Honey Hollow Bouldering and the Pit Boulders.

ca_lake_ramona.blurb: Lake Ramona is a hilltop and hillside boulder field northwest of the lake in North San Diego County, reached on foot with a long approach. Roughly 150 boulder problems are spread over South Slope, Summit Area, Sub-Summit, North Slope and the Base Area, and some boulders also carry trad or top-rope lines. Boulder problems run from V0 to V11, concentrated between V2 and V5, with a good number at V7 and above. The roped lines add grades from 5.7 to 5.13, with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.11.

ca_santa_ana_mountains.blurb: The Santa Ana Mountains rise along the eastern edge of the Los Angeles Basin, mostly within Cleveland National Forest. Bouldering dominates, about three quarters of the climbs, on short rock; a few crags add small single-pitch sport, trad and top-rope lines. Boulder problems mostly run from V0 to V4, with a handful harder, and roped lines run roughly 5.7 to 5.11. El Cariso is the largest section, mostly boulders, while Ortega Falls adds top-rope walls and trad on a granitic outcrop beneath a seasonal waterfall that flows mainly after winter storms. KinderCare Boulders and San Juan Canyon also hold boulders.
